newsitem.title: CHINA: Mitsubishi Motors in China auto venture.
newsitem.headline: Mitsubishi Motors in China auto venture.

text.p: Mitsubishi Motors Corp has received approval to set up a joint venture to make all-terrain vehicles in China's southern Hunan province, a company official said on Tuesday.
"The project has been approved by the provincial State Planning Commission in Hunan," a project official at Mitsubishi's Beijing office told Reuters.
The official said the venture was registered in Yongzhou and would be built in nearby Lengshuitan.
Mitsubishi was expected to take about 25 percent of the venture, which would have an initial annual production capacity of 10,000 vehicles, Hong Kong's South China Morning Post said.
The rest would be held by an unidentified vehicle plant under the People's Liberation Army, local officials said.
"There is such a project. It is registered in Yongzhou city," an official of the Administration for Industry and Commerce said by telephone from the provincial capital, Changsha.
The South China Morning Post said the approval came despite the central government's unofficial announcement that it would not approve any more new foreign-funded car plants.
The newspaper quoted a Hunan official as saying the joint venture had won permission because it would turn out a vehicle currently not produced in China.
Annual production capacity of the venture could expand to 30,000 a year, the Post quoted the official as saying.
Mitsubishi was considering floating the venture but had no timetable, the official said.
